To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have developed a novel framework for the analysis of large-scale quantitative metabolomics data, which we called NET analysis.

we have developed a novel method for mechanistic analysis of quantitative metabolite data and have demonstrated the method's ability to infer functional principles of metabolism and to resolve intracellular metabolite concentrations from averaged metabolome data.
NET analysis can (1) identify putative regulatory sites, (2) identify reactions that are subject of allosteric regulation, and (3) identify metabolites that are subject of genetic regulation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of methods for the computational analysis of biological data, with a focus on metabolomic data.
the development of novel mathematical models for the description of biological systems.
developing methods for analyzing metabolome data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
NET analysis is a powerful tool for the functional analysis of large‐scale quantitative metabolic data and that it is a valuable complement to other omic analysis tools.
NET analysis is an extremely useful tool to gain insights into the regulatory principles of metabolism.
NET analysis is a powerful framework to integrate metabolome data into the analysis of metabolic networks and cellular function.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

NET analysis allows us to unravel the functional role of the metabolite level in a network‐embedded thermodynamic framework and to integrate it into our systems biology data‐based analysis of living organisms.

the integration of quantitative metabolome data into a thermodynamically operating network provides a unique opportunity to gain mechanistic insight into the functional principles of metabolic networks.
NET analysis is an excellent tool to identify and quantify the regulatory potential of metabolite concentrations in cellular networks.
The main takeaway from our work is that

quantitative metabolomics data can be integrated into metabolic network models and analyzed with thermodynamic constraints to gain insights into the regulation and dynamics of the underlying cellular networks.
the thermodynamic framework of NET analysis allows to identify and quantify active regulatory sites in a network.
quantitative metabolome data can be used for the identification of putative regulatory sites in metabolic networks.
